Subject: Private deployment capacity targets + topology questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood Private last week. We're heading into our procurement window and want to lock on throughput targets and basic topology assumptions before we start sizing racks. A few concrete asks:

- Target sustained QPS: we'd like guidance for both a conservative and optimistic forecast.
- Preferred autoscale behavior: how quickly can an on-prem pool absorb a 5x burst and what warm-pool assumptions do you make?
- Network: what NIC / crossconnect recommendations should our network team provision (bandwidth, MTU, jumbo frames, latency SLAs)?

We've attached our current traffic profile and a draft network diagram (see attachments). Happy to hop on a call but wanted to capture this in writing.

Best,
Daniel

Hi Daniel — great to get this. I reviewed the attachments; a few quick notes up front, and I'm looping in our infra and SRE leads for the sizing math.

Short answers:
- Conservative sustained target: 2000 reqs/s (single-tenant, low-multiplex)
- Optimistic sustained target: 8000 reqs/s (with multiplexing, KV prefix caching, and light model quantization)
- Burst absorption: with a warm pool strategy and pre-warmed KV caches, a properly-sized Dedicated pod can absorb ~3–5x for short windows (30–120s) before admission control trims low-priority traffic.
- Network: recommend 25–100 Gbps per rack depending on pod size, MTU 9000 where supported, and crossconnect latency under 1ms for rack-to-rack; avoid chaining >2 top-of-rack switches for pod fabrics.

Attachments: we prepared a short capacity sweep (capacity-sweep.xlsx) and updated diagram (network-diagram-v2.pdf) with our default topology.

Next steps: Jonas, can you validate the rack/NIC guidance and give a concrete GPU/slot mix for their optimistic and conservative cases? Rishi, can you add the autoscale cooldowns and admission-control defaults we should propose? Laura, I'll need you to review the pricing impact if they choose the optimistic config.

Thanks — Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private deployment capacity targets + topology questions

Thanks for the context, all. I dug into HelioRx's traffic sample (spike histogram + p90 latency target) and sketched two rack-level configs. Key assumptions first:

- Model: 30B transformer, FP16 / int8 path available (we assume quantization for optimistic case).
- Request mix: 65% short generative queries (avg 60 tokens), 35% long-context retrievals (KV cache hit rate ~= 40% after warmup).
- Latency target: p95 < 250ms for generative lane.

Conservative build (sustained 2k req/s):
- 4 racks, each rack = 4x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (16 GPUs total)
- NICs: 25 Gbps per host (oversubscription 2:1 at ToR), aggregate rack egress ~400 Gbps headroom
- Expected steady throughput: ~1.8–2.4k req/s depending on batching and cache hit
- Warm pool: keep 2 pods warm per rack for sub-60s absorption

Optimistic build (sustained 8k req/s):
- 12 racks, each rack = 8x H100-equivalent GPUs (96 GPUs total)
- NICs: 100 Gbps per host preferred for horizontal scaling, ToR spine with 400G uplinks
- Required egress: ~1.2–1.6 Tbps headroom across fabric (depends on replica topology)
- Multiplexing: we assume multiplex factor 8–12 for short queries; KV cache hit target 60–70%

Notes on tradeoffs:
- If HelioRx cannot provide jumbo frames or low-latency crossconnects, we must increase GPU count to hit latency SLOs (latency penalty ~10–25% with small MTU/extra hops).
- Admission control: with optimistic config, we can prioritize production traffic and still offer best-effort dev/test lanes.

I'll attach a quick rack math export to the drive link and updated diagram notes.

-Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment capacity targets + topology questions

Quick SRE response with autoscale and stability knobs: 

- Autoscale cadence: control-plane signals + local pod telemetry. We recommend a two-stage scale: fast ramp (add pods, 15–45s) and slow ramp for full GPU re-provisioning (3–8 minutes) depending on hypervisor image boot time.
- Warm-pool strategy: maintain a small warm pool of pre-initialized containers with KV cache 'peeked' against a sample prompt set. Warm pool size depends on expected burst: for 5x short bursts, a warm pool equal to ~25% of production pods yields ~80% absorption without admission control.
- Admission control defaults: p99 throttle at 5s queue depth for non-critical routes; route tags to separate dev/test.
- Cache priming: recommend daily/lightweight cache priming during off-peak to sustain high hit rates; include a background job to periodically refresh top prefixes.
- Failure modes: network flaps cause cache invalidation. We add a grace period and write-through logic so hot KVs are rebuilt incrementally rather than full eviction.

I'll add these defaults to the shared spreadsheet (capacity-sweep.xlsx) and note the cooldowns and SLOs.

-Rishi
SRE Manager
Redwood Inference

Daniel — summary and next steps below. Please confirm the checklist items and we'll turn this into a formal sizing quote and run a short PoC if you want: 

Summary (what Redwood recommends):
- Conservative: 16 GPUs (4 racks x 4 GPUs) targeting ~2k req/s sustained; recommended NIC: 25G per host; warm pool: 2 pods/rack.
- Optimistic: 96 GPUs (12 racks x 8 GPUs) targeting ~8k req/s sustained with multiplexing; recommended NIC: 100G per host; fabric egress target ~1.2–1.6Tbps.
- Autoscale: fast ramp 15–45s (containers/pods), slow ramp 3–8min (full GPU reprovision). Warm pool sizing = ~25% of prod pods to cover ~5x short bursts.
- Network: MTU 9000 preferred, avoid >2 ToR hops, latency rack-to-rack <1ms for p95 latency SLO.
- Ops compromises: if HelioRx cannot meet network targets, we recommend stepping up GPU count ~20–30% or lowering the multiplex target.

Action items (owners):
- HelioRx: confirm target p95/p99 latency and whether jumbo frames are allowed (Daniel) — due 2026-11-27.
- Redwood infra: produce final rack-level quote and unit economics for both configs (Jonas, due 2026-11-30).
- Redwood SRE: finalize autoscale cooldowns and warm-pool runbook (Rishi, due 2026-11-29).
- Redwood sales: produce pricing delta and commitment options for both builds (Laura, due 2026-11-30).

Attachments: network-diagram-v2.pdf (updated topology), capacity-sweep.xlsx (math & cost delta).

If HelioRx wants a short PoC we can stand up a limited pool in our staging colo and run a 2-hour burst test to validate numbers.

Thanks all — Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering
